purpose: Correlates TMICC's own disclosed strategic decisions against the same-window competitor and macro-commodity timeline, so a strategist sees not just what TMICC did but what happened around it

timeline.event: Ferrero Group agrees to acquire Wells Enterprises (Blue Bunny, Bomb Pop, Halo Top) — baseline context predating this window
Cocoa futures hit an all-time high, briefly over $11,530/tonne in London — the peak of the 2024-2025 cocoa crisis

Ben & Jerry's Homemade, Inc. files suit against Conopco, Inc. (Unilever's US subsidiary) in the Southern District of New York, alleging Unilever silenced the brand's public statements calling for a Gaza ceasefire — the opening move in a governance dispute that continues past TMICC's own demerger a year later.
Ben & Jerry's publicly states Unilever has "muzzled" the brand over statements on Trump and other contentious political topics, extending the dispute beyond the original Gaza-ceasefire claim.
Unilever's ice cream division and General Mills reported discussing ice cream market trends together, months before the TMICC demerger
CEO David Stever departs. Ben & Jerry's alleges he was ousted for supporting the brand's independent board; Unilever frames the departure as part of a broader restructuring.
Global cocoa grinding fell nearly 5% year-on-year (Asia down 16%) as consumers cut back or switched to lower-cocoa formulations under sustained high prices
Jochanan Senf appointed Ben & Jerry's new CEO.
CNBC: chocolate prices still rising but 2026 outlook signalled as 'sweeter' — early sign of the price relief that materializes by late 2026

First Capital Markets Day — CEO/CFO engaged directly with the top 50 shareholders; announced a target dividend payout ratio of 40-60%; presented the sustainability framework later formalized in the listing Prospectus

Co-founder Jerry Greenfield steps down, stating Unilever has "silenced" the brand's social mission. Separately, Ben & Jerry's co-founders write to the Board of the soon-to-launch TMICC asking that the brand be made fully independent.
Board member appointment date recorded in the Annual Report's governance section (appointee's exact identity needs verification — see docs/magnum_ecosystem.md gap)
A pro-Gaza-themed ice cream flavor is blocked by leadership, per Ben & Jerry's own account of events.
Trade press: 'Froneri's success shows why Unilever is right to spin off ice cream' — competitor strength cited as validating the demerger, a month before it closed
Demerger from Unilever completed
MICC begins trading on Euronext Amsterdam, LSE, and NYSE; initial market value ~$9.1bn
First round of fresh analyst ratings and outlook commentary published on MICC post-listing
FIL Limited (Fidelity) discloses a 19,894,021-share position
Trade roundup 'Major Dairy Industry Deals' names General Mills alongside Lactalis, Fonterra, Unilever, and Arla in the same wave of dairy-sector M&A activity around the TMICC demerger
BlackRock Inc. discloses a 25,965,010-share position
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. discloses a 20,026,031-share position

TMICC removes all independent directors from Ben & Jerry's board — chair Anuradha Mittal plus Jennifer Henderson and Daryn Dodson among those forced off, applying retroactive term limits and a new code of conduct introduced after the demerger.
TMICC files a Memorandum in Opposition arguing the removed directors had become "ineligible" to serve under the new rules; Ben & Jerry's seeks a court injunction to halt the board restructuring.
MICC closes at its all-time high of $19.87 — the day before its first maiden results as a standalone company

First maiden full-year (FY2025) results as a standalone company: mixed and messy — sharp declines in annual earnings and cash flow, profit below forecast, driven partly by one-off separation costs. Underlying disclosed detail: 380bps of commodity/supply-chain cost inflation (cocoa + a stronger euro named specifically), offset by a productivity programme and select pricing actions; Italy performance 'below par' with an explicit business reset; capex up 11% YoY to 4.5% of revenue; restructuring: a net €40m provision release plus €50m of supply-chain-optimisation costs
Shares 'melt' on the maiden results — AJ Bell: 'Magnum's meltdown: can Unilever's ice cream spin-off recover from a bad start?'
Allan & Gill Gray Foundation discloses a 19,674,251-share position

In its own FY2025 annual results, Nestlé announces 'advanced negotiations' to sell its remaining ice cream businesses (Asia, Canada, parts of Latin America — ~SFr1bn/$1.2bn revenue) to Froneri, targeted to complete by early 2027. CEO Philipp Navratil calls ice cream 'a distraction' from Nestlé's pivot to coffee and petcare. No plan to exit the Froneri JV itself (Nestlé keeps its 50% stake)
'Unilever-Magnum Ice Cream Company spin-off winner' retrospective published — framing the Nestlé exit news against TMICC's own rocky week, one week after t17/t18
KPMG Accountants N.V. signs the audited FY2025 Annual Report in Amstelveen (engagement partner C.M.L. Priem RA) — the full, detailed disclosure document this ecosystem/timeline research is built from
The Ben & Jerry's Foundation wins a court ruling allowing it to join the lawsuit against Unilever/TMICC over the company's contractual obligations to the brand's independence.
Former Ben & Jerry's independent board chair Anuradha Mittal files a defamation lawsuit against Unilever/TMICC.

TMICC completes its acquisition of Kwality Wall's in India (plus a Portugal marketing/sales entity, 1 Apr 2026) — India enters TMICC's reporting perimeter from Q2 2026. A real, closed acquisition, not a stated ambition.

Q1 2026 Trading Update: AMEA delivers +7.9% organic sales growth (volume and price both contributing); Turkiye and Pakistan post double-digit growth; China posts high-single-digit growth. 'Frontline First' execution model cited as delivering across At-Home and Away-from-Home channels; Digital Commerce maintains double-digit growth.

AGM: Resolution 5, adopting a new executive incentive structure ('Foundation Plan for Growth' — personal co-investment by senior leaders with real downside risk, not a broad growth-strategy document despite the name), passes with 77.37% in favour but 22.63% against — over the UK Corporate Governance Code's 20% threshold that legally requires a public update statement on shareholder engagement, which followed on 17 Sept 2026 (see below). A real, dated proxy-governance friction signal, separate from the Ben & Jerry's dispute but in the same broad category: governance scrutiny of TMICC's leadership.
A consumer boycott threat tied to the governance dispute puts TMICC on the defensive — real reputational-risk materialization for one of its most values-driven, activist consumer-base brands.

General Mills sells its Häagen-Dazs retail and gifting shop business in mainland China to an investor consortium including tea-chain operator Ningji, while retaining ownership of the Häagen-Dazs foodservice business there — a localization/control-ceding move in a complex market
The lawsuit reaches what trade press describes as a "crucial stage."

H1 2026 results announced: revenue EUR4.7bn (H1 2025: EUR4.5bn), organic sales growth +4.7% (volume +2.5%, price +2.2%). All three regions contributed — Europe & ANZ +4.1%, Americas +3.2% (a real acceleration from FY2025's +0.8%), AMEA +7.6% (still fastest-growing, though decelerating from FY2025's +10.9%). Management reaffirms full-year guidance of 3-5% OSG and 40-60bps margin improvement.

Within the H1 2026 results (see t54): the productivity programme delivered EUR90m of savings in H1 2026 alone (EUR70m supply chain, EUR20m overheads) - 18% of the EUR500m medium-term target reached in a single half-year, management says the programme 'remains on track.' This is the first real progress figure disclosed against that target since it was set in 2024.

Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream, Inc. — Froneri's real US entity, the business Froneri bought from Nestle in the 2019 deal already noted in the ecosystem doc — voluntarily recalls select lots of Outshine frozen fruit bars (Strawberry, Watermelon, Grape, Tangerine, Black Cherry) over possible glass contamination, distributed nationwide.

Judge P. Kevin Castel (Southern District of NY) rules on the Ben & Jerry's board lawsuit: dismisses 7 of 10 claims (plus part of an 8th) — mostly the claims about Ben & Jerry's speech, board composition, and director appointment/removal. Two claims survive in full: missed payments under a 2022 settlement, where Unilever had agreed to pay Ben & Jerry's two installments of $2.5m each (arising from licensing the Ben & Jerry's trademark in the Occupied Palestinian Territories without the Independent Board's approval) and allegedly didn't. TMICC formally replaces Unilever as defendant for the surviving claims.

Cocoa prices have retreated to roughly $4,000/tonne from the June 2024 peak of $11,530 — real relief on the exact commodity headwind TMICC's FY2025 results blamed for margin pressure. But early surveys of the 2026/27 West African crop (harvest begins October) show below-average cherelle formation — a weak-start signal that could reopen the same pressure

The Ben & Jerry's Foundation states its operations are at risk of suspension unless funding is restored - a real operational-continuity consequence of the same funding dispute underlying TMICC's 15 Sept 2026 'toxic culture' filing (t59), not just a reputational or legal matter anymore.

MICC trades at $19.50, market cap $11.99bn — up roughly 32% from the $9.1bn IPO valuation and back near its all-time high, a full recovery from the Feb 2026 "meltdown" low of $12.94 (52-week range: $12.94-$20.69).

Lakeland Dairies — TMICC's own named milk supplier under the Caring Dairy standard — is fined GBP115,000 for pollution at its Artigarvan site, a real environmental-compliance incident against a direct TMICC supplier.
timeline.source: surfaced via fetch_competitor_news.py, Ecosystem & partners column

timeline.event: TMICC's court filing alleges former chair Anuradha Mittal was "abusive, discriminatory and unprofessional," fostered a toxic board culture, appointed personal contacts over independent candidates, and directed roughly $350,000 from the Ben & Jerry's Foundation to the Oakland Institute, a nonprofit she founded. Mittal's camp responds that this is a retaliatory "campaign to intimidate, threaten, and character assassinate" her over her advocacy for Palestinian human rights, naming activist investor Nelson Peltz as displeased by that advocacy specifically. Both sides' claims are disputed and unresolved as of this pass — presented here exactly as each side has filed/stated it, not as established fact either way.

TMICC publishes its required shareholder-engagement update statement following the May 2026 AGM's 22.63% dissent on the executive incentive resolution (t62), as mandated by the UK Corporate Governance Code.

correlation_patterns.title: TMICC's rocky debut and Nestlé's exit announcement landed one week apart
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: TMICC's maiden results melted the stock on 12 Feb 2026; Nestlé's CEO called ice cream 'a distraction' and moved to exit further just 7 days later, on 19 Feb. Both are FY2025 annual-results announcements, so the timing overlap could simply be shared reporting season rather than one causing the other — but it's a real, dated coincidence worth watching: does a second major player's public retreat from the category further pressure how the market reads TMICC's own standalone story?

correlation_patterns.title: Two competitors ceded direct local control within four months of each other
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: Nestlé is exiting ice cream operations in Asia/Canada/Latin America to Froneri (Feb 2026), and General Mills sold its China retail/gifting shops to a local consortium while keeping foodservice (Jun 2026) — both are large multinationals ceding direct operational control of ice cream in complex markets while retaining brand/licensing value. TMICC runs the opposite structure in some of its own complex markets (majority-controlled JVs in the Philippines: Magnum RFM, Selecta) — worth tracking whether that full-control model outperforms or underperforms the peer trend toward local-partner handoff.

correlation_patterns.title: The exact commodity headwind TMICC blamed for FY2025 margin pressure is now easing
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: TMICC's FY2025 results explicitly named cocoa inflation (plus a stronger euro) as a driver of 380bps of cost inflation, offset by pricing actions and a productivity programme. Cocoa has since retreated from its 2024 peak to roughly a third of that level by Sept 2026 — the next thing to watch for is whether TMICC's FY2026 commentary shows margin recovery or a reversal of the pricing actions taken during the high-cost period. The 2026/27 crop-season risk flag (weak early crop signals) is the one thing that could reopen this pressure before it's resolved.

correlation_patterns.title: Board upheaval and the market meltdown landed five weeks apart
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: TMICC stripped Ben & Jerry's entire independent board on 1 Jan 2026; five weeks later, on 12 Feb 2026, TMICC's own maiden results melted the stock. No source ties the two together directly, and reporting-season timing is a genuine alternative explanation for the market reaction — but a strategist should still ask whether governance turmoil contributed to investor unease in that specific window, since both were real, dated, and close together.

correlation_patterns.title: The stock fully recovered; the governance dispute never did
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: By Sept 2026 MICC sits near its all-time high, market cap up ~32% from IPO — yet the Ben & Jerry's dispute escalated the entire time: a defamation suit (Mar), a boycott threat (May), the lawsuit narrowing with TMICC taking over as defendant (Aug), and a fresh "toxic culture" filing (Sept). Worth asking directly: is the market rationally judging Ben & Jerry's as immaterial to group earnings, or under-pricing a real brand/reputational risk that hasn't yet shown up in the numbers?

correlation_patterns.title: AMEA is both the fastest-growing and by far the most profitable region
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin: AMEA 22.9% vs Europe & ANZ 13.1% and Americas 14.1% — while AMEA also posted the fastest organic sales growth both in FY2025 (+10.9%) and H1 2026 (+7.6%, still far ahead of the other two regions even as it decelerates). This directly validates the Group strategy's specific 'Accelerate share growth in China' initiative (see the Strategy tab) — the numbers make a real case for weighting future capital allocation toward AMEA even more heavily than the current strategy documents suggest.

correlation_patterns.title: India is TMICC's fastest volume growth story and its clearest near-term margin drag, at the same time
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: TMICC is building 4 new factories in India after sales growth exceeded 50%, and CEO Peter ter Kulve has openly attributed 'current weak profitability' there to cold-chain and freezer-cabinet investment in a developing market. That's a real, disclosed trade-off, not a hidden one - but it sits directly underneath the Group's medium-term 40-60bps margin-improvement commitment. Worth watching whether India's margin drag has a stated end-date, or whether it's open-ended as long as volume growth continues.

correlation_patterns.title: The EUR500m savings target is running well ahead of a simple straight-line pace
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: EUR90m in one half-year is 18% of the full multi-year EUR500m target already. A simple annualized read (EUR90m x roughly 5-6 half-years to reach EUR500m) would land TMICC ahead of its own 'medium-term' framing - though half-year progress rarely stays linear (early wins are often the easiest), so this is a pace worth re-checking next half-year, not a number to extrapolate confidently yet.

correlation_patterns.title: Two separate governance-scrutiny threads ran in parallel through 2026, and both are about the same underlying question: who actually controls TMICC's decisions
correlation_patterns.strategist_note: The Ben & Jerry's board dispute (independence from TMICC) and the 22.63% AGM dissent on the executive incentive plan (alignment between TMICC's leadership and its shareholders) are legally and factually unrelated - but both are real, dated instances of a governance stakeholder pushing back on how TMICC's leadership exercises control, in the same year. A strategist tracking 'is TMICC's governance under more scrutiny than peers' should treat these as two data points on the same question, not two unrelated footnotes.
